articles.author: Sam Ro
articles.headline: Companies Are Cashing In On Consumers' Unwillingness To Bargain Shop
articles.summary: Award-winning Financial writer Sam Ro says "this contradiction helps explain why, despite poor vibes, the economy continues to grow, profit margins continue to expand, and corporate earnings continue to rise."
articles._summary: Sentiment surveys confirm that consumers are very aware of rising prices, and they are complaining about them. People hate inflation. Interestingly, inflation hasn't really stopped people from spending. Economic data confirm this . A recent research note from Goldman Sachs highlights studies reflecting these trends. "After-tax corporate profits as a share of value added have roughly doubled from about 5% in the late 1980s to over 10% recently," Goldman economists wrote. "Over the same period, U.S. firms have substantially raised markups — the amount by which prices exceed the marginal cost of producing goods and services." At least some of this trend toward rising markups over the years can be explained by falling costs . Regardless, the point is that what customers are paying increasingly covers much more than the costs. But why hasn't there been more pushback from consumers ?
articles._zh_headline: 公司正在利用消费者不愿在商店讨价还价的现象获利
articles._zh_summary: 情绪调查证实，消费者非常清楚价格上涨，并且对此有所抱怨。人们讨厌通货膨胀。有趣的是，通货膨胀并没有真正阻止人们消费。经济数据证实了这一点。高盛最近的一份研究报告重点介绍了反映这些趋势的研究。高盛经济学家写道：“税后企业利润占增加值的比例大约翻了一番，从 20 世纪 80 年代末的 5% 左右增至最近的 10% 以上。” “在同一时期，美国公司大幅提高了加价幅度，即价格超过生产商品和服务的边际成本的幅度。”多年来这种加价上涨的趋势至少可以用成本下降来解释。无论如何，关键是客户支付的费用越来越多，远远超出了成本。但为什么消费者没有更多的抵制呢？
